description: THE LEFT-TRUNCATING MOVE AT :224, AND THE ONLY CASE IN THIS DIRECTORY WHOSE RESIDUAL BALANCE IS NOT ZERO. The complete bill payment again - WHEN 'Y' at app/cbl/COBIL00C.cbl:174 of the ordered EVALUATE CONFIRMI at :173-191, reaching :211-235 in full - but driven by a TEN-INTEGER-DIGIT balance, which is the one input shape under which MOVE ACCT-CURR-BAL TO TRAN-AMT at :224 LOSES A DIGIT and the single COMPUTE at :234 therefore yields something other than zero. SERVICE. case15 is the canonical happy path and states in its own text that this lossy shape is this file's subject and is not generalised from there; this file is that subject, worked out in full. WHY THIS MATTERS MORE THAN IT LOOKS. Every other case in this directory that reaches :234 carries a balance below 1,000,000,000.00 - case15 pays 194.00, case16 pays 843.00, case18 pays 55.00 - and for all of them the move at :224 is LOSSLESS, so :234 computes x - x and stores exactly 0.00. An implementation that ignored the picture difference between the sender and the receiver would pass all of those and still be wrong. Without this case the program's only COMPUTE is never asserted against anything but zero, which proves almost nothing about the arithmetic (gate G28). WHAT THIS FILE ASSERTS, AND WHAT IT DELIBERATELY DOES NOT. A ParityCase carries ONE screenRequest, which is one invocation, so it can state at most one arm of any one EVALUATE - the constraint case17 records and the reason it encodes a single arm. Two of this program's remaining arms cannot be reached in the same invocation as this one and are NOT claimed here: the 'You have nothing to pay...' branch at :197-206 is the OPPOSITE side of the very IF this case's balance decides, and the NOTFND and WHEN OTHER arms of UPDATE-ACCTDAT-FILE at :390-402 would leave the account UNWRITTEN, which is precisely the record this case exists to pin. Both are described below with their exact induction recipe and their verified byte images, so whichever file takes them needs no re-derivation and no reader is left inferring what this one covers (practice B12). THE SITE, AND THE TWO PICTURES THAT DISAGREE. :224 MOVE ACCT-CURR-BAL TO TRAN-AMT moves ACCT-CURR-BAL, declared PIC S9(10)V99 at app/cpy/CVACT01Y.cpy:7 - TEN integer digit positions and two fraction positions, twelve character positions in the record - into TRAN-AMT, declared PIC S9(09)V99 at app/cpy/CVTRA05Y.cpy:10 - NINE integer digits and two fraction positions, ELEVEN character positions. The receiver is one integer digit narrower than the sender, and nothing in the program tests for it: there is no ON SIZE ERROR clause anywhere in COBIL00C's 572 lines and no validation of the moved amount at all. THE RULE, AND ITS DIRECTION. A numeric MOVE aligns sender and receiver on their IMPLIED DECIMAL POINT, so the digits that do not fit are dropped from the HIGH-ORDER end: COBOL truncates a PIC 9 item on the LEFT and a PIC X item on the RIGHT. The two directions are not interchangeable and this program contains both, three lines apart: the alphanumeric moves at :222, :223, :227, :228 and :229 pad and truncate on the right - 'POS TERM' into X(10), the 21-character 'BILL PAYMENT - ONLINE' into X(100), 'BILL PAYMENT' into X(50), 'N/A' into X(50) and into X(10) - while :221 MOVE 2 TO TRAN-CAT-CD zero-fills PIC 9(04) on the left to 0002 and :224 discards on the left. A translation that used plain assignment for :224 would keep the digit COBOL throws away. THE ARITHMETIC, DIGIT BY DIGIT AND WITHOUT A STEP OMITTED. The seeded balance is 1,234,567,890.12 - ten integer digits, the widest ACCT-CURR-BAL can hold. Stored in the record it is the twelve bytes 12345678901B: the twelve digits 123456789012, of which the first ten are the integer part 1234567890 and the last two the fraction 12, with the trailing '2' replaced by 'B' because 'B' is the positive overpunch carrying a low-order digit of 2. :224 moves it into nine integer digits, so the HIGH-ORDER '1' - worth 1,000,000,000.00 - is DISCARDED and TRAN-AMT receives 234,567,890.12, stored as the eleven bytes 2345678901B. :234 COMPUTE ACCT-CURR-BAL = ACCT-CURR-BAL - TRAN-AMT then subtracts what was actually stored, not what the balance was: 1,234,567,890.12 - 234,567,890.12 = 1,000,000,000.00 EXACTLY, which is the place value of the discarded digit and nothing else. The rewritten record therefore holds the twelve bytes 10000000000{ - eleven digits and the positive-zero overpunch '{' - and the account is left owing a billion dollars after a payment that reported success. THAT IS WHAT THE COBOL DOES AND IT IS NOT REPAIRED HERE (practice B5). If an implementation produces 00000000000{ here it has not modelled the move at :224 at all. THE OVERPUNCH BYTES ARE VERIFIED, NOT GUESSED. A signed DISPLAY item occupies exactly p + s character positions and the sign occupies none of its own; it is overpunched into the TRAILING byte, which is the only reading under which CVACT01Y sums to 300 and CVTRA05Y to 350. The tables are '{ABCDEFGHI' for digits 0-9 positive and '}JKLMNOPQR' for digits 0-9 negative, taken from FixedWidthRecord.ZonedSign rather than from memory. Pinning the stored image rather than a decimal literal pins the overpunch byte itself: the unsigned form 100000000000 decodes to the same quantity while not being what COBOL writes into a signed DISPLAY item, and '}' is a different byte from '{'. THE SCALE AND THE ROUNDING MODE, NAMED (gates G23 and G24). Both operands and both receivers are SCALE EXACTLY 2 - a V-scale scan of all 28 copybooks returns only V99 - and neither is ever a double or a float (AAP rule R4). The COMPUTE at :234 carries NO ROUNDED phrase, and the keyword ROUNDED appears ZERO TIMES across all 28 programs, verified by exhaustive search of app/cbl. COBOL therefore TRUNCATES excess fractional digits on store, so in Java the subtraction is exact and the store is BigDecimal.setScale at scale 2 with RoundingMode.DOWN, which common/CobolDecimal names once as COBOL_ROUNDING and which nothing else in the module names. HALF_UP, HALF_EVEN, CEILING and FLOOR ARE ALL WRONG (AAP rule R2). The left truncation is the same seam: CobolDecimal.storeAtPicture truncates the fraction DOWN and then discards high-order digits by remainder ten-to-the-p, which is how a COBOL receiver with no ON SIZE ERROR behaves - it wraps quietly rather than reporting. THE SUB-CENT ASSERTION, AND WHY IT IS MADE AT THE SEAM AND NOT HERE (practice B12). RoundingMode.DOWN is only distinguishable from a nearest-value policy when a THIRD decimal digit is non-zero, and no record field in COBIL00C can carry one: ACCT-CURR-BAL and TRAN-AMT are both declared V99, the wire format is fixed width, and a third fraction digit has no character position to occupy. Fabricating a scale-3 record field to manufacture the assertion would be inventing a layout the copybooks do not declare. The discrimination is therefore asserted where it is reachable - at the CobolDecimal seam every monetary store in BillPaymentService routes through - and it IS asserted rather than quietly dropped: BillPaymentServiceTest.excessFractionDigitsAreDropped supplies 10.005, 10.009 and 0.999 to the scale-2 receiver and pins 10.00, 10.00 and 0.99, where HALF_UP would have produced 10.01, 10.01 and 1.00, and CobolDecimalTest pins 10.415 to 10.41 for the same reason. That is stated plainly because omitting the assertion would let gate G24 pass vacuously, and claiming this file made it would be a claim about a span that does not exist. NO PACKED DECIMAL IS INVOLVED. Verified: NO copybook in this repository declares COMP-3 or PACKED-DECIMAL, so every persisted numeric field is zoned DISPLAY and the codec needs no nibble unpacking anywhere in the record layer. The WS-ABS-TIME PIC S9(15) COMP-3 at :59 is working storage, is consumed by EXEC CICS FORMATTIME at :255-261 and is never persisted. WHY THE ACCOUNT ROW IS INLINE, AND WHY THE FIXTURE WAS NOT EDITED (practice B3). No shipped fixture row can supply this balance. app/data/ASCII/acctdata.txt holds 50 rows of exactly 300 bytes and every one of them carries a '{' overpunch in the trailing byte of ACCT-CURR-BAL with a zero tens-of-cents digit, giving whole-dollar balances from 2.00 to 843.00 - the largest is three integer digits, seven short of what :224 needs to lose anything. Editing the fixture to manufacture a ten-digit balance is refused outright: the reference tree is the parity oracle and not one byte of app/cbl, app/cpy, app/cpy-bms, app/bms, app/csd or app/data is written by this migration. So ACCTDAT is seeded INLINE, and the row is app/data/ASCII/acctdata.txt ROW 0 WITH EXACTLY ONE SPAN REPLACED: ACCT-CURR-BAL goes from the shipped 00000001940{ to 12345678901B and all twelve other spans are byte-identical to the shipped row, taken from it by slicing rather than retyped. ACCT-ID stays 00000000001, so the keyed read at :345-354 addresses the identifier ACTIDINI supplies and the cross-reference at :410-418 addresses the same one, exactly as the single MOVE with two receivers at :170-171 arranged. NOTHING IN THE ROW IS BUSINESS-INCONSISTENT IN A WAY THE PROGRAM CAN SEE: COBIL00C never reads a credit limit - the strings ACCT-CREDIT-LIMIT and CREDIT-LIMIT appear ZERO times in its 572 lines - so leaving ACCT-CREDIT-LIMIT at the shipped 20200.00 below the balance changes no branch and asserts no business rule, while raising it would be inventing data the program never looks at. THE 'YOU HAVE NOTHING TO PAY' BRANCH: UNREACHABLE FROM THE SHIPPED DATA, AND NOT CLAIMED HERE. :197-206 is IF NOT ERR-FLG-ON / IF ACCT-CURR-BAL <= ZEROS AND ACTIDINI OF COBIL0AI NOT = SPACES AND LOW-VALUES, and on this case's balance of 1,234,567,890.12 the first term is FALSE, so the branch does not fire, no flag is raised, and :208 opens the payment block. Reaching it needs a balance at or below zero, which as counted above NO fixture row has, so it needs inline rows of its own and the condition is <= ZEROS, so it needs BOTH sides: a balance of exactly 0.00, which is the twelve bytes 00000000000{ - positive zero, and a different byte from the '}' of negative zero and the '0' of an unsigned rendering - and a negative balance, for which the verified images are 00000000010} for -1.00, whose low-order digit 0 overpunches to '}', and 00000000000J for -0.01, whose low-order digit 1 overpunches to 'J'. Those images are recorded here because they are derived and checkable, not because this file asserts them. Note also what the condition's second and third terms are worth: if ACTIDINI were blank, the EVALUATE at :158-167 would already have set the error flag and :197 would not open at all, so in practice the guard is REDUNDANT - and it is preserved exactly as written, because removing a term that can never be false is still a change to the program (practice B5). THE REWRITE, ITS THREE ARMS, AND WHICH ONE IS HERE (gates G47 and G30). :235 PERFORM UPDATE-ACCTDAT-FILE reaches :377-403, which issues EXEC CICS REWRITE DATASET(WS-ACCTDAT-FILE) FROM(ACCOUNT-RECORD) LENGTH(LENGTH OF ACCOUNT-RECORD) RESP(WS-RESP-CD) RESP2(WS-REAS-CD) - with NO RIDFLD, so it replaces the record the read-for-update at :351 is still holding, which is the one place in the program where the UPDATE option is used for what it is for - and then an EVALUATE whose arms are, IN SOURCE ORDER, WHEN DFHRESP(NORMAL) at :388 with a body of CONTINUE, WHEN DFHRESP(NOTFND) at :390-395, and WHEN OTHER at :396-402 LAST. THIS FILE PINS THE FIRST ARM, which is what makes the rewritten 300-byte record observable at all. THE OTHER TWO, RECORDED RATHER THAN ASSERTED: NOTFND moves 'Account ID NOT found...' - the THIRD and last call site in the program that emits that exact text, the others being READ-ACCTDAT-FILE at :361, which case17's sibling arm covers, and READ-CXACAIX-FILE at :425, which case18 covers - and it is distinguishable from both because by the time it fires the TRANSACT write at :512-520 has ALREADY SUCCEEDED, so a transaction row exists while the balance rewrite failed. WHEN OTHER first emits DISPLAY 'RESP:' WS-RESP-CD 'REAS:' WS-REAS-CD at :397 and then moves 'Unable to Update Account...' - capital Update, capital Account, three dots. Both are INDUCED, not wished for: the model carries a forcedOutcomes map keyed by repository operation, so 'rewrite' with outcome NOT_FOUND drives AccountRepository.WriteResult.notFound and 'rewrite' with outcome OTHER drives a write result carrying an unexpected file status, exactly as case17 induces its read failure through 'readForUpdate'. THEY CANNOT BE CO-ASSERTED HERE: a rewrite that does not land records nothing on the ACCTDAT WRITES channel and leaves the seeded row unchanged in the final state, so the residual balance this case exists to pin would vanish from the expectation. AND THE CONSEQUENCE WORTH WRITING DOWN FOR WHOEVER TAKES THEM: UPDATE-ACCTDAT-FILE is the LAST paragraph of the payment block at :235, so its message is the last thing assigned to WS-MESSAGE before the unconditional send at :242 - the user sees the error even though the transaction was written and the success string had already been composed - and nothing in the program ever resets ERRMSGC, so the DFHGREEN set at :526 by the successful write is still in force while the text is an error. That is a genuine legacy inconsistency and it must be preserved, not tidied. THE CROSS-REFERENCE READ, AND WHY IT IS A FINDER AND NOT A TABLE (gate G45). :211 performs READ-CXACAIX-FILE, which at :410-418 is EXEC CICS READ DATASET(WS-CXACAIX-FILE) INTO(CARD-XREF-RECORD) LENGTH(LENGTH OF CARD-XREF-RECORD) RIDFLD(XREF-ACCT-ID) KEYLENGTH(LENGTH OF XREF-ACCT-ID) RESP RESP2 - note the ABSENCE of UPDATE, because nothing rewrites this record - and the EVALUATE at :420-436 takes WHEN DFHRESP(NORMAL) at :421 / CONTINUE. app/csd/CARDDEMO.CSD defines CXACAIX as an ALTERNATE INDEX TO CCXREF VIA ACCOUNT KEY over the CCXREF base cluster, so in Java it is ONE repository with a second finder on the eleven-byte alternate key and never a second table. The row supplies XREF-CARD-NUM for the move at :225 and nothing else; it is read and never written, which is why the cross-reference appears in inputs and in normalisations and in NEITHER expectedWrites nor expectedFinalState nor expectedDatasets. THE CROSS-REFERENCE ROW INDEX IS 48, AND IT WAS COMPUTED BY SLICING (gate G16, risk R-F). app/data/ASCII/cardxref.txt is ordered by its BASE key, XREF-CARD-NUM ASCENDING, so the zero-based row index for an account is emphatically not the account number minus one; slicing bytes 26-36 of every row locates account 00000000001 at ROW 48, carrying customer 000000001 and card 9680294154603697, which is the value TRAN-CARD-NUM receives. AND THE ROWS ARE SEEDED AT 36 BYTES, DELIBERATELY UNPADDED. app/cpy/CVACT03Y.cpy declares fifty - XREF-CARD-NUM X(16) at 1-16, XREF-CUST-ID 9(09) at 17-25, XREF-ACCT-ID 9(11) at 26-36 and FILLER X(14) at 37-50 - and the fixture omits that trailing FILLER, making it the one fixture of the nine that is not faithful to its copybook. parity/FieldDiffer is the declared SOLE OWNER of the 36-to-50 right-pad, applied once at seed time through the CARDXREF_FILLER_PAD_36_TO_50 normalisation this case declares against CXACAIX; pre-padding the rows here would double-apply it and produce a 64-byte row. THE TRANSACTION MASTER IS INLINE BECAUSE NO FIXTURE FOR IT EXISTS. app/data/ASCII holds exactly nine files and none of them is a transaction master - README.md lists it as not applicable, because it is populated online - so TRANSACT is declared inline at the copybook's own 350 bytes rather than by asking for a tenth fixture. The seeded row is what INITIALIZE TRAN-RECORD leaves behind for everything but its identifier, since the EXEC CICS READPREV at :474-482 reads only the key from it: alphanumeric spans are spaces, TRAN-CAT-CD and TRAN-MERCHANT-ID are zero-filled, and TRAN-AMT is the positive zero 0000000000{. HIGH-VALUES, THE BROWSE, AND THE IDENTIFIER ARITHMETIC. :212 MOVE HIGH-VALUES TO TRAN-ID fills the PIC X(16) key with the highest value the collating sequence has, which is recorded as an UNANCHORED BACKWARD BROWSE rather than encoded as a key literal, because what CICS does with a high-values RIDFLD is position past the last record. :213 STARTBR-TRANSACT-FILE takes WHEN DFHRESP(NORMAL) at :452, :214 READPREV-TRANSACT-FILE takes WHEN DFHRESP(NORMAL) at :485 and leaves the highest-keyed row in TRAN-RECORD, and :215 ENDBR-TRANSACT-FILE at :503-505 is a BARE EXEC CICS ENDBR WITH NO RESP OPTION AND NO EVALUATE AT ALL - an absence that is preserved and not repaired, so no failure arm is invented for it and the expectation records no outcome for it. :216 MOVE TRAN-ID TO WS-TRAN-ID-NUM moves X(16) into the PIC 9(16) at :57 at EQUAL width, so no digit is lost, and :217 ADD 1 TO WS-TRAN-ID-NUM is the program's only non-monetary arithmetic. The seeded master holds 0000000000000041, so the sum is 0000000000000042: the increment lands in the units position with no carry, and nowhere near the sixteen-nines boundary where a PIC 9(16) receiver with no ON SIZE ERROR clause would discard its high-order digit and wrap to zeros. That identifier pair is chosen deliberately to match BillPaymentServiceTest.leftTruncationLeavesANonZeroBalance, which drives this same balance through the same service, so the declarative expectation and the executable assertion can be read side by side. THE 350-BYTE RECORD, SUMMED FROM app/cpy/CVTRA05Y.cpy RATHER THAN FROM PROSE (practice B11). TRAN-ID X(16) at 1-16, TRAN-TYPE-CD X(02) at 17-18, TRAN-CAT-CD 9(04) at 19-22, TRAN-SOURCE X(10) at 23-32, TRAN-DESC X(100) at 33-132, TRAN-AMT S9(09)V99 at 133-143, TRAN-MERCHANT-ID 9(09) at 144-152, TRAN-MERCHANT-NAME X(50) at 153-202, TRAN-MERCHANT-CITY X(50) at 203-252, TRAN-MERCHANT-ZIP X(10) at 253-262, TRAN-CARD-NUM X(16) at 263-278, TRAN-ORIG-TS X(26) at 279-304, TRAN-PROC-TS X(26) at 305-330 and FILLER X(20) at 331-350 - which is 350, the RECLN the copybook's own header states (gate G19). :218 INITIALIZE TRAN-RECORD runs first and then the eleven moves at :219-229 in SOURCE order, which is not copybook order: :225 moves TRAN-CARD-NUM before :226 moves TRAN-MERCHANT-ID, while the copybook declares the merchant items ahead of the card number. The field map below is in COPYBOOK DECLARATION ORDER, because that is the order the record's bytes are in and the order a field-for-field diff walks. FILLER X(20) IS PINNED, AS TWENTY SPACES (gate G21): it is an addressable span and not a gap, and since nothing follows it the TOTAL WIDTH is the only thing that can catch its absence, which is why the complete image is pinned alongside the fourteen named fields. THE 300-BYTE ACCOUNT RECORD, SUMMED THE SAME WAY FROM app/cpy/CVACT01Y.cpy. ACCT-ID 9(11) at 1-11, ACCT-ACTIVE-STATUS X(01) at 12, ACCT-CURR-BAL S9(10)V99 at 13-24, ACCT-CREDIT-LIMIT at 25-36, ACCT-CASH-CREDIT-LIMIT at 37-48, ACCT-OPEN-DATE X(10) at 49-58, the misspelled ACCT-EXPIRAION-DATE X(10) at 59-68, ACCT-REISSUE-DATE X(10) at 69-78, ACCT-CURR-CYC-CREDIT at 79-90, ACCT-CURR-CYC-DEBIT at 91-102, ACCT-ADDR-ZIP X(10) at 103-112, ACCT-GROUP-ID X(10) at 113-122 and FILLER X(178) at 123-300 - which is 300, the RECLN the copybook's header states (gate G19). ACCT-EXPIRAION-DATE IS MISSPELLED IN THE COPYBOOK AT CVACT01Y.cpy:11 AND IS MISSPELLED HERE (requirement I1): correcting it to ACCT-EXPIRATION-DATE would leave the diff looking for a span the decoder never produces, which is a silent parity break rather than a loud one. THE OFFSET TRAP, VERIFIED BY SLICING: offsets 103-112 hold 'A000000000' and that span is ACCT-ADDR-ZIP, while ACCT-GROUP-ID at 113-122 holds TEN SPACES. FILLER X(178) IS PINNED, AS 178 SPACES (gate G21). ONLY ACCT-CURR-BAL DIFFERS BETWEEN THE SEEDED ROW AND THE REWRITTEN ONE, from 12345678901B to 10000000000{. THE EDITED BALANCE, WHICH IS FOURTEEN BYTES AND IS TRANSIENT. :193 MOVE ACCT-CURR-BAL TO WS-CURR-BAL and :194 MOVE WS-CURR-BAL TO CURBALI OF COBIL0AI run inside the :169 guard and outside the EVALUATE, so they fire on this arm too and leave exactly +1234567890.12 in CURBALI. WS-CURR-BAL is PIC +9999999999.99 at :56 - a sign position, ten integer positions, an actual decimal point character and two fraction positions, fourteen bytes and an exact fit for the symbolic map's CURBALI PIC X(14) at app/cpy-bms/COBIL00.CPY:66 - and this is the ONE rendering in the program wide enough to show all ten integer digits, which is worth noting precisely because TRAN-AMT is not. THOSE FOURTEEN CHARACTERS ARE NOT WHAT THE SENDS CARRY, and that is not a contradiction: :524 blanks the field again before either send happens, so the edited image is asserted where it survives - on the lookup-and-prompt cases - and pinning it on a send here would assert a screen the program never transmits. THE 26-BYTE TIMESTAMP, DERIVED AND THEN PINNED. :230 performs GET-CURRENT-TIMESTAMP at :249-267: EXEC CICS ASKTIME ABSTIME(WS-ABS-TIME), then EXEC CICS FORMATTIME ABSTIME(WS-ABS-TIME) YYYYMMDD(WS-CUR-DATE-X10) DATESEP('-') TIME(WS-CUR-TIME-X08) TIMESEP(':'), then INITIALIZE WS-TIMESTAMP, MOVE WS-CUR-DATE-X10 TO WS-TIMESTAMP(01:10), MOVE WS-CUR-TIME-X08 TO WS-TIMESTAMP(12:08) and MOVE ZEROS TO WS-TIMESTAMP-TM-MS6. app/cpy/CSDAT01Y.cpy declares WS-TIMESTAMP as 9(04) + FILLER '-' + 9(02) + FILLER '-' + 9(02) + FILLER ' ' + 9(02) + FILLER ':' + 9(02) + FILLER ':' + 9(02) + FILLER '.' + 9(06), which sums to 26 with separators at bytes 5, 8, 11, 14, 17 and 20. THE DERIVATION THAT MATTERS: IBM COBOL's INITIALIZE does NOT touch FILLER items, so all six separators SURVIVE it; bytes 1-10 are then overwritten with YYYY-MM-DD, bytes 12-19 with HH:MM:SS and bytes 21-26 with 000000. BYTE 20 IS THEREFORE A PERIOD - not a space and not a digit - and the microseconds are ALWAYS 000000, because the MOVE ZEROS at :266 is unconditional and nothing in the program ever writes a sub-second value. The image is 2022-07-19 23:12:32.000000, exactly 26 characters. :231-232 MOVE WS-TIMESTAMP TO TRAN-ORIG-TS TRAN-PROC-TS is ONE MOVE WITH TWO RECEIVERS, both PIC X(26), so the two spans hold the IDENTICAL twenty-six bytes: this program has no separate processing time, and a translation that derived the second from a second clock reading would differ here. DETERMINISM (practice B7). The instant is PINNED to 2022-07-19T23:12:32 - the instant this program's own version footer at :571 carries, and the same instant every other case in this directory pins - and it is supplied by the injected Clock that common/DateHeader reads, never by a captured now. ANY 26-BYTE TIMESTAMP WRITTEN TO TRANSACT COMES FROM THAT FIXED VALUE. A captured one would make this case pass once and fail on the next run, and would poison two spans of the written record at once. Two-digit month, day and hour, no midnight and no daylight-saving edge, so the MM/DD/YY and HH:MM:SS renderings POPULATE-HEADER-INFO derives from the same instant - 07/19/22 and 23:12:32 - are unambiguous and mutually consistent with the image above. Those six header items are POPULATE-HEADER-INFO's at :319-338 and belong to BillPaymentController rather than to the service under test, so a SERVICE case does not claim them. US-ASCII is named explicitly rather than left to a platform default, which for a nine-fixture ASCII corpus and a twelve-dataset EBCDIC one is the difference between a comparison and a coincidence (practice B8). WRITE, THEN COMPUTE, THEN REWRITE - AND THE ORDER IS THE BEHAVIOUR. :233 PERFORM WRITE-TRANSACT-FILE, :234 the COMPUTE, :235 PERFORM UPDATE-ACCTDAT-FILE, in that sequence and no other. The consequence is observable and is this program's most likely misreading: the transaction is written carrying the PRE-PAYMENT amount, and the balance is only reduced afterwards. On this case the point is sharper than on any sibling, because the amount written is not even the pre-payment balance - it is the pre-payment balance MINUS ITS HIGH-ORDER DIGIT - so TRAN-AMT 2345678901B, ACCT-CURR-BAL before 12345678901B and ACCT-CURR-BAL after 10000000000{ are three DIFFERENT twelve- and eleven-byte images, and no two of them can be substituted for one another. The order is asserted structurally as well as by value: expectedWrites carries the TRANSACT record at write position 0 and the ACCTDAT record at write position 0 of its own dataset, and expectedDatasets states one row on each WRITES channel. THE SUCCESS ARM, IN SOURCE ORDER, AND THE SCREEN IT LEAVES BLANK. :512-520 is EXEC CICS WRITE DATASET(WS-TRANSACT-FILE) FROM(TRAN-RECORD) LENGTH(LENGTH OF TRAN-RECORD) RIDFLD(TRAN-ID) KEYLENGTH(LENGTH OF TRAN-ID) RESP RESP2, and the EVALUATE at :522-547 takes its first arm, WHEN DFHRESP(NORMAL) at :523, whose body runs in an order that is itself the point. :524 PERFORM INITIALIZE-ALL-FIELDS runs FIRST, and at :560-566 that paragraph is MOVE -1 TO ACTIDINL followed by one MOVE SPACES with FOUR RECEIVERS - ACTIDINI, CURBALI, CONFIRMI and WS-MESSAGE - each blanked at its own declared width. SO THE SUCCESSFUL SCREEN SHOWS A BLANK ACCOUNT IDENTIFIER (eleven spaces), A BLANK BALANCE (fourteen spaces) AND A BLANK CONFIRMATION (one space), even though the record's balance was just updated. Note what is NOT blanked - ERRMSGO, which keeps whatever the last send put there until the next send overwrites it, which is exactly what lets this arm blank WS-MESSAGE and then compose a confirmation into it. :525 MOVE SPACES TO WS-MESSAGE is not redundant: STRING overlays from the receiver's first byte and does NOT blank the tail. The cursor is ACTIDINL, from that MOVE -1 at :562; -1 is CURSOR METADATA and not payload - an xxxL length item is how COBOL positions the cursor - so it is declared as cursorField and not as a screen field. THE CONFIRMATION TEXT, COUNTED CHARACTER BY CHARACTER. :527-531 is STRING 'Payment successful. ' DELIMITED BY SIZE ' Your Transaction ID is ' DELIMITED BY SIZE TRAN-ID DELIMITED BY SPACE '.' DELIMITED BY SIZE INTO WS-MESSAGE. Both literals are DELIMITED BY SIZE, so each contributes EVERY character it has including the TRAILING space of the first and the LEADING space of the second - which is why TWO CONSECUTIVE SPACES separate 'successful.' from 'Your'. TRAN-ID is DELIMITED BY SPACE, which takes the characters up to but not including the first space, and a sixteen-digit zero-padded identifier contains none, so ALL SIXTEEN DIGITS contribute. The result is exactly 'Payment successful.  Your Transaction ID is 0000000000000042.' - 20 + 24 + 16 + 1 = 61 characters. :293 then moves the 80-byte WS-MESSAGE over the 78-byte ERRMSGO, so the value asserted on each send is those 61 characters left-justified and space-padded to exactly 78; the two-byte loss is the picture difference between PIC X(80) and PIC X(78) and not a shortened expectation, and with 17 spaces to spare nothing of the text is cut. TWO SENDS, ONE MESSAGE, AND AN EMPTY MESSAGE CHANNEL. :532 PERFORM SEND-BILLPAY-SCREEN is send #1, from inside the WRITE's success arm. Control then returns to :234 and :235, and :242 PERFORM SEND-BILLPAY-SCREEN fires again UNCONDITIONALLY - it sits after the END-IF at :240, so it runs on both halves of the :210 branch - which is send #2. WS-MESSAGE still holds the confirmation and ERRMSGC still holds DFHGREEN, so the two sends are identical in every field and both are asserted; the program has 19 PERFORM SEND-BILLPAY-SCREEN sites and this single invocation legitimately reaches two of them, the send COUNT is itself behaviour, and a translation that suppressed the duplicate as a tidy-up would differ here (practice B5). expectedMessages IS EMPTY, and that is a deliberate assertion rather than an omission: that channel is for lines a program EMITS, which in this codebase means COBOL DISPLAY, and all six DISPLAY sites in COBIL00C - :366, :397, :430, :461, :490 and :541 - sit in a WHEN OTHER arm of a file operation, while this path takes the NORMAL arm of every one of the six RESP-tested operations it performs.
